title: kv-cache attention kernel & seqlen edge-case debug notes
content:
Summary:
Quick personal notes while debugging the regression reported on 2026-02-24: responses truncating / hallucinating when sequence length crosses ~4096 tokens for some models (gpt-medium-ish family). Suspect interaction between KV cache indexing and attention kernel selection (kernel switches at certain seqlen thresholds).

High-level hypothesis:
- Serving runtime picks different attention kernels depending on sequence length and model dtype/quantization (e.g., flash_attn vs. cuBLAS/aten fallback).
- KV cache layout or indexing assumptions differ between kernels (offsets, shape ordering), causing stale / misaligned KV reads when kernel switch occurs mid-stream or for long prefixes.
- Edge-case arises when prefix length + generation length > kernel threshold -> partial writes/read out-of-bounds or wrong stride.

Repro steps I used locally (conda env: ri-dev, commit: pr/3421 patch applied):
1) Start local runner with small batch size and single GPU (A100):
   ./run_local.sh --model rwinf/gpt-medium --port 5050 --num-workers 1
2) Send following prompt with a long prefix to force >4096 tokens:
   python tests/send_request.py --url http://localhost:5050/generate --prompt-file tests/long_prefix.txt --max-tokens 512 --stream=false
3) Observed output differs from baseline after ~4096th token; sometimes repeats earlier sentence or crashes with index error.

Commands / instrumentation added:
- Inserted logging around kernel selection: serving/runtime/inference/attention_selector.cpp -> logs kernel name + input seqlen + kv_cache.shape each request.
- Added KV cache checksum helper (simple XOR of float32 bytes per key slab) and logged before/after kernel calls.
- Ran unit test suite with seqlen loop: python -m pytest tests/test_kv_cache.py::test_seqlen_transitions -k "4096 or 4097 or 8192"

Representative logs (sanitized):
[2026-02-24 16:12:03] request_id=abcd kernel=flash_attn seqlen=4094 kv_shape=(12, 2, 4094, 64) checksum=0x9f12e3
[2026-02-24 16:12:03] request_id=abcd kernel=aten_attn seqlen=4098 kv_shape=(12, 2, 4098, 64) checksum=0x9f12e3
[2026-02-24 16:12:04] request_id=abcd ERROR attention_index_mismatch: kv_read_offset=4094 kv_write_offset=0

Error snippets seen in worker logs:
- RuntimeError: index out of bounds for dimension 2 at /pytorch/aten/src/... (stack truncated)
- Warning: KV cache checksum mismatch after aten_attn call (expected 0x9f12e3 got 0x7a44b0)
- GPU OOM when trying to allocate fallback buffers for aten_attn at seqlen 8192 (only occurs in quantized path)

What I tried so far (and results):
1) Force a single kernel (always flash_attn) by overriding selector config -> bug disappears for many runs.
   - Conclusion: kernel boundary is involved.
2) Force the other kernel (always aten_attn) -> bug is present for long seqlen but consistent; KV checksums differ in different places (indicates layout / stride mismatch).
3) Added explicit fence/sync around KV writes before switching kernels -> reduced incidence but did not eliminate; suggests a timing/race is not the only cause.
4) Reproduced with synthetic toy model (small dims) in Python CPU path by simulating two kernel implementations with different indexing assumptions -> mismatch reproduced deterministically.

Narrowed hypotheses (ranked):
1) Kernel implementations expect different KV layout (e.g., contiguous vs. blocked layout). When the runtime writes cache assuming layout A but then invokes kernel B, kernel B reads incorrect memory offsets.
2) Seqlen-based padding/trimming code uses exclusive vs inclusive endpoints depending on kernel path. Off-by-one leads to misalignment at threshold.
3) Quantized models produce different stride/packing of KV (packed into int8 blocks) and kernel selection doesn't trigger unpack path correctly.
4) Rare race with async memcpy when switching kernels under concurrency (less likely given deterministic repro in synthetic CPU sim).

Files/locations to inspect next:
- serving-runtime/src/kv_cache_manager.* (write/read layout contracts)
- serving-runtime/src/attention_kernels/* (flash_attn.cc, aten_attention.cc) -> look for assumed strides / view() calls
- runtime/config/kernel_selector.yaml (thresholds and overrides)
- tests/test_kv_cache.py (add more exhaustive seqlen boundary cases: 4095,4096,4097,8191,8192,8193)

Quick checks to run (manual):
- Compare memory layout: print(kv.storage().data_ptr()) and strides for both writer and kernel view inside a small repro.
- Add assert in kernel entry: assert(kv.dim(2) == expected_seqlen) and assert(strides match) to catch mismatch early.
- Create a small repro that writes KV with layout A then tries to read with layout B and assert failure (I already did this in toy model).

Temporary mitigations to deploy if this is customer-impacting:
- Force a single kernel for affected models via kernel_selector override (config flag per-model) until root cause fixed.
- Reject requests that would cross the problematic seqlen boundary (e.g., cap prefix length) - last resort.

Longer-term fixes to consider:
- Define strict KV cache ABI (document in confluence link) and enforce with runtime assertions / unit tests.
- Unify kernel interfaces to accept an explicit stride/format descriptor instead of implicit assumptions.
- Add golden tests in CI that run both kernels for a variety of sequence lengths and compare outputs / checksums.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why does flash_attn and aten_attn differ only at certain dtype/quantization combos? Need to run same seqlen switch across fp16, bf16, int8 quantized paths.
- Are there model-specific packing optimizations (e.g., rotary embedding packing) that interact with KV shape?
- Is there any historical reason we allowed kernels to assume layout (maybe for perf) - who owns that decision? ask @Ethan Cole.

Next actions (short):
- [0.5d] Add detailed asserts at kernel entry to fail fast and surface first mismatch location.
- [0.5d] Add unit tests for seqlen boundaries in tests/test_kv_cache.py and CI job to run them on PRs.
- [1d] Diff strides/memviews between writer and reader in the runtime for a failing repro and paste here.
- [1d] If ABI mismatch confirmed, start PR to add explicit KV format header (small struct) and update both write/read code paths + tests.

Notes to self:
- Keep reproducer minimal and environment stable (single process, single GPU). Concurrency masks some deterministic bugs and makes debugging slower.
- Save all kernel logs under /tmp/kv-debug/<timestamp> for postmortem and attach to JIRA.

Attached quick paste of the toy repro Python used (sanitized):
```
# toy_kv_layout_repro.py
import numpy as np
# writer writes (num_heads, 2, seqlen, head_dim) contig
writer = np.arange(12*2*4097*64, dtype=np.float32).reshape((12,2,4097,64))
# reader expects blocked layout (num_heads, 2, seqlen//4, 4, head_dim)
reader_view = writer.reshape((12,2,4097//4,4,64)) # mismatched reshape -> deterministic wrong reads
assert reader_view.shape != writer.shape
print('toy repro shows shape mismatch -> reproduces off-by-layout behavior')
```

If anyone sees a quicker way to detect layout mismatch at runtime (cheap checksum or lightweight shuffling), shout out in slack #infra-kv-debug.

End of notes.
